page.overview:
Who is Bahariasaurus?

(meaning "Bahariya lizard") is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived in North Africa during the Late Cretaceous period around 95 million years ago. Very little is known about Bahariasaurus as only a small number of hipbones have been found. Even those were lost, however, when Allied bombs destroyed the German museum where the bones were housed during WWII.

A number of these bones were found by German paleontologists shortly before WWI. In the early 1930's they were named Bahariasaurus and identified as coming from a huge carnivore. WWI ended the original search for the specimen and WWII destroyed what had been found. Some scientists have suggested that Bahariasaurus may have been part of the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/tyrannosaurid Tyrannosauridae] family. However, no Tyrannosauroid has been recorded in Africa. Others believe that Deltadromeus should be a junior synonym of Bahariasaurus.

Bahariasaurus was featured in the Jurassic Park Institute now available to browse on Dinopedia.
